_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Nuclear Surety Evaluation (NSE)
summary: The Nuclear Surety Evaluation (NSE) is a technical report developed by a nuclear weapons System Program Office to document compliance with Nuclear Safety Design Certification requirements in a Certification Requirements Plan.
use_relationship:
A Nuclear Surety Evaluation (NSE) is a technical report developed by a nuclear weapons System Program Office (SPO) to document compliance to all Nuclear Safety Design Certification (NSDC) requirements identified in a respective Certification Requirements Plan (CRP). The CRP defines the requirements, assigns the roles and responsibilities, and defines all the activities and tasks required to achieve Nuclear Certification. The CRP is created to meet the needs of a particular acquisition or modification effort. As program changes are encountered and incorporated into the acquisition or modification effort, their impact on the nuclear certification process is reviewed and the CRP is updated accordingly. The Program Manager-approved CRP contains all required details regarding how and when the program office will meet the certification requirements. Nuclear Safety Design Certification requirements are listed in a Certification Requirements Matrix (CRM) within the Safety Design section of the CRP. The NSE provides the Air Force Safety Center with the analyses of the work the contractor completes to meet or exceed compliance with Nuclear Safety Design Certification requirements in Air Force Manual (AFMAN) 91-118, Safety Design and Evaluation Criteria for Nuclear Weapon Systems and Department of the Air Force Manual (DAFMAN) 91-119, Safety Design Criteria for Nuclear Weapon Systems Software, and guidance in Department of the Air Force Instruction (DAFI) 91-101, Air Force Nuclear Weapons Surety Program. The NSE also describes the weapon system, the specific components, assembly, or systems analyzed, methods used, and concerns resulting from analyses performed.
This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format and content preparation information for the deliverable resulting from the work task described in the solicitation and contract. This DID is related to NPFC - DI-NUOR-81409, Certification Requirements Plan (CRP), AFMAN 91-118, DAFMAN 91-119, and DAFI 91-101. (Copies of DAFIs, DAFMANs, and AFMANs are available online at http://www.e-publishing.af.mil/.) The U.S. Navy is excluded from requirements set forth in this DID.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The NSE shall be in contractor's format, following the outline provided within this document.

children.title: The NSE shall be limited in scope to a single certification action but shall not limited in length.
children.content: A certification action is a piece of new equipment or an already-certified piece of equipment in need of modification that interfaces with nuclear weapon system and requires Nuclear Safety Design Certification.

children.title: The NSE shall define the component, assembly, or system analyzed.
children.content: It shall include identifying information such as item identification numbers and item uses/description.

children.title: The NSE shall include a summary of engineering analysis, demonstration, inspection, and test
children.content: through technical qualitative reports, technical quantitative reports, photos, videos, diagrams, schematics, graphs, and sketches.

children.title: The NSE shall include approved deviations as outlined in DAFI 91-101.
children.content: Note: all deviations must be approved prior to Nuclear Safety Design Certification being granted.

children.title: The NSE shall be specific enough to demonstrate to the Air Force Safety Center, Weapons Division (AFSEC/SEW) that the SPO meets the Nuclear Safety Design criteria agreed to in the CRP.
Outline
children.content: For hardware and/or software (as applicable) provide:

children.title: Certification Action Information
SPO recommendation of "Certification" or "Certification with Restrictions"
Item Identification
Hardware or Software designation
Nomenclature or Common Name
National Item Identification Number (NIIN)
Manufacturer and Manufacturer Code
Model/Part Number/Software number
Weapons used with
Item Manager/Nuclear Certification Manager (NCM)/POC Information
Uses and Description
Equipment uses
Interface with Critical Functions
Technical Orders with identified Nuclear Surety Procedures (NSP)
Relevant Non-Analytical Information
Summary of AFMAN 91-118 and DAFMAN 91-119 Requirement Compliance
Requirement compliance shown through engineering analysis, demonstration, inspection, and test.
children.content: Requirement compliance shall be provided in either report format or CRP Matrix format. Either format is acceptable provided the submitter addresses every CRP line item for compliance. See Appendix A of this document.

children.title: When required by the CRP, the submitter provides a Critical Signal Analysis (CSA) for DAFMAN 91-119 compliance.
children.content: See Appendix B of this document.

children.title: Deviations and Recommended Restrictions
Provide approved Nuclear Surety Deviations for this certification action.
Provide any recommended restrictions from the summary of requirement compliance captured in the document.
Appendix A - Proof of Nuclear Safety Design Certification Compliance
Either in report format or CRP matrix format, identify the specific AFMAN 91-118 and/or DAFMAN 91-119 criteria.
children.content: The content of the appendix shall reference line items in the compliance matrix within the CRP for traceability. The purpose is to show how the program has complied with every compliance matrix requirement specified within the CRP for AFMAN 91-118 and DAFMAN 91-119.

children.title: Cite each document and paragraph used (e.g., test plans, reports, bent pin analysis) to show compliance with each AFMAN 91-118 and/or DAFMAN 91-119 requirement.
children.content: Discuss the verification methods used to justify the compliance.

children.title: These references can be submitted as attachments to the NSE.
Specify deficiencies against compliance for which a deviation has not been approved.
Appendix B - Critical Signal Analysis
Provide the following in the Critical Signal Analysis:
Flow of Critical Signals from human intent to critical function activation
All components between human intent and critical function activation
The potential effect those components could have on the Critical Signal
The protection mechanisms provided to Critical Signals
